findings.title: Require exact historical source/audit bytes for every nonselected attempt
findings.evidence: The attempt loop copies extant local files, but resolves recorded historical hashes only for .py inputs. It records source/audit metadata without requiring the original or snapshot hash to exist. A missing or changed failed source/audit snapshot can therefore escape the stated all-history completeness gate. Selected PASS bytes are checked separately and are not affected.
findings.minimal_change: For each historical source/audit field present, resolve its recorded SHA through original/snapshot or preserved history, require equality, publish the exact bytes with original aliases, and record those explicit bindings. Retain raw records unchanged.

findings.title: Account for attempts rejected before verification.json exists
findings.evidence: Only verification.json directories are recursively archived. Existing non-stale pipeline attempts are not required to have a proof record or an explicit no-record classification; only direct driver/dependency files beside pipeline.json are retained. Thus a terminal precompiler rejection can leave nested output unaccounted for by the stated attempt-history completeness gate.
findings.minimal_change: For every pipeline attempt, bind an existing raw proof record, or explicitly classify and preserve all available output as a precompiler/no-verification attempt from the actual driver status and logs; reject unexplained omissions. Never fabricate verification.json or a compiler invocation.
